beliefs.practice: Use a single shared Mongoose connection pool per Node process and configure maxPoolSize (e.g., 50) in the Mongo URI/options; never open/close a connection per HTTP request.
Do not commit credentials to source; keep DOCUMENTDB_URI out of the repo and use a secret store (Azure Key Vault) in production, with a .env.example placeholder for local dev.

Open change streams with a filtered aggregation pipeline (use $match on ns.coll or on operationType and specific fields) and set fullDocument:'updateLookup' only when you need the whole doc; persist resumeTokens so restarts resume where they left off.

Model each trade as a single document with a transitions subdocument array (each entry: {from,to,timestamp,user,metadata}) and also write an append-only transition log collection for audit and efficient querying.

Use multi-document transactions via startSession/withTransaction to atomically advance state and write a transition log; keep transactions small (few docs, small byte size) and short-lived to avoid timeouts.

Set appropriate writeConcern and readConcern for transactional work (use writeConcern: { w: 'majority' } and readConcern: 'local' or 'majority' per consistency requirements) and ensure driver options include retryWrites=true for transient server errors.

Index all fields used in filters and group keys for aggregation endpoints: create single or compound indexes on assetClass, counterpartyId, and settlementDate (e.g., { assetClass:1, counterpartyId:1, settlementDate:-1 }).

For vector search, create a vector index on the vector field with dimension and algorithm parameters (HNSW/IVF/M parameter and efConstruction) appropriate to your vectors, and ensure the field type is stored as a dense numeric array in documents.

Limit full-document lookups and heavy aggregations in change stream handlers; offload expensive work to a worker queue and acknowledge/record the event before long-running processing to avoid change stream stalls.
Persist and version the change stream resume token (e.g., in a small control collection or external durable store) after processing each batch so restarts can resume without data loss.
Set Mongoose option autoIndex: false in production and build indexes as part of deployment/ops, not at app startup, to avoid RU spikes and long startup delays.

Choose a partitioning/partition key aligned with your hottest query patterns (e.g., counterpartyId or assetClass) to avoid cross-partition queries for frequent transactions and to keep transactional work within a partition when required.
Keep transactions and state documents small to stay under engine limits (limit number of operations and document size inside a transaction) and fail fast if size thresholds are approached.

Use exponential backoff and idempotent retry semantics in application code for transient network or rate-limit errors; surface transient failures to a retry middleware that caps retries and logs the incident.

Avoid scatter/gather queries that touch many partitions for the aggregation endpoint; if the aggregation is frequent/heavy, maintain pre-aggregated counters (materialized views) updated in the same transaction or via a low-latency change stream worker.
Tune index keys for cardinality: put the most selective fields first in compound indexes (e.g., {counterpartyId:1, assetClass:1, settlementDate:-1}) and avoid indexing low-cardinality booleans alone.

Instrument operations with telemetry (request/response latency, RU consumption, transaction commits/aborts) and export to Azure Monitor/Log Analytics so you can alert on RU throttling, high latency, and repeated transaction aborts.

Use TTL indexes on transition log / ephemeral collections to automatically purge old audit entries (create TTL index on a timestamp field with the desired expiration seconds), rather than manual deletes.

When running change streams against a managed/cloud Mongo-compatible host, limit the change stream visibility window by checkpointing frequently and avoid keeping a very long-running cursor without checkpoints to reduce chance of resumability gaps.

Fail early when incompatible MongoDB server features are required (check server wire version / featureCompatibilityVersion at startup) and gate features like advanced vector index options or new transaction semantics behind runtime checks.
